verdict.rationale: Shopify's agent surface is built on UCP. The UCP spec describes AP2 payment mandates and verifiable credentials that let agents "transact on behalf of users with pre-defined, verifiable boundaries," with signed payment authorizations "mathematically tied to the specific state of the cart." That implies scoped, cart- and merchant-bound credentials rather than a raw card. However, Shopify's own checkout docs only show negotiated payment handlers (e.g. com.google.pay) and a requirement that a "payment credential has been collected." They never document AP2 mandate support, user-set amount caps, or credential expiry. Missing for 10: Shopify-documented support for AP2 mandates in its checkout, explicit amount-limit and expiry controls on the payment credential, explicit merchant-restriction configuration, and any hands-on evidence of a scoped-credential checkout.
